prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind O&M; scope Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere); excludes public grid, non-farm port ops. Wildmere: Export Limit Advisory→Grid Dispatcher when capability<target; applies accepted ceiling, records time; keeps protection settings unless authorized switching plan. Turbine Controller (Glassfin): validated commands within protections, blocks conflicts, safe mode on auxiliary loss; Pitch Deviation Notice. Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor→Turbine Sensor Bus. Offshore Substation (Morrowick): Main Transformer, export cable, Export Cable Monitor, station service transformers, Fire Detection Panel; Transformer Tap Snapshot→Shore Control Room; mode Substation Degraded. Substation Operator: switching after state check + Control Engineer authorization; notifies Grid Dispatcher. Emergency Generator (Foxglove): auto-start on auxiliary loss, no unapproved paralleling; Start Test Trace. SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale): telemetry→Shore Control Room (Amber Quay); Session Revocation Receipt→Cybersecurity Gateway. Shore Control Room: keeps last validated limit on comms loss; Switching Window Acknowledgment; incident log. Grid Dispatcher priority safety>protection>export. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard): Position Quality Flag. Mode Grid Constraint: Duty Planner records basis; Control Engineer reduces stepwise, restores after authorization. Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown): Squall Window Bulletin, Deferred Task Rationale; identifies reschedulable tasks under uncertain visibility. Weather Service→Weather Analyst (Wave Burst Record, Visibility Confidence Note)→Duty Planner (uses for readiness/pause/defer). Metocean Buoy: local reference vs forecast; discrepancies prompt review of age/location. Assessment records visibility estimate+confidence; low confidence = constraint; point estimate insufficient if plausible range unsafe; visual-alignment work assessed conservatively; Blade Inspection Drone deferred if visibility uncertain. Go/no-go: method, competence, vessel, confidence. Duty Planner: Transfer Manifest Addendum→Vessel Master. CTV: Harness Audit Card. SOV: Recovery Basket Load Sheet. Personnel: Marine Coordinator expected count; North/South Access Scanner; Personnel Tracking Console verified total; discrepancy→pause transfers. SCADA Engineer verifies Firmware Hash Attestation. Emergency: Rescue Coordinator leads; Vessel Master may withdraw; Field Supervisor site control; HSE Officer advises; Control Engineer remote shutdown, technical guidance on recovery affecting turbines. Mode Turbine Lockout until authority confirms safe. Recovery: Rescue Coordinator objective, checks Load Sheet; Marine Coordinator assigns vessels,

New part:
S677: The Vessel Master retains authority to proceed, slow, alter course, or hold position based on actual conditions and vessel limits.
S678: A Crew Transfer Vessel may be directed to remain clear of a transfer location until the crew and vessel can maintain adequate visual awareness.
S679: A Daughter Craft operation requires particular caution where reduced visibility could compromise separation from other vessels or structures.
S680: A Service Operations Vessel may maintain a safe stand-off while the visibility assessment is clarified.
S681: Planned vessel movements account for reduced speed, increased separation, and the possibility of returning to a safe holding area.
S682: When uncertainty increases during transit, the Marine Coordinator and Vessel Master reassess the route and the suitability of continuing toward the work site.
S683: The Shore Control Room maintains awareness of the decision and the operational restrictions associated with the assessment.
S684: A no-go decision is appropriate when uncertainty prevents the team from demonstrating that the transfer or task can be completed within safe limits.
S685: Conditions are reassessed before work resumes, and authorization is based on current evidence rather than the earlier estimate.
S686: The inventory record covers serviceable parts, consumables, repairable units, and their locations across shore and offshore stores.
S687: Warehouse System maintains the authoritative item catalogue, stock balances, and storage locations.
S688: Stock visibility includes quantities on hand, items reserved for approved work, and quantities already committed to transfer.
S689: Spares Hub provides a separate view of stock held for regional replenishment and emergency support.
S690: The Storekeeper reconciles physical counts with recorded balances and records adjustments with a reason and timestamp.
S691: Each stocked item is identified by a controlled part number, description, unit of measure, and approved substitute status.
S692: Serial-controlled parts retain traceability from receipt through installation, repair, return, or disposal.
S693: Reservations prevent the same available quantity from being assigned to multiple work packages.
S694: Maintenance Planning Engine uses planned work demand and part criticality to support replenishment forecasts.
S695: The Duty Planner reviews forecast demand against current stock before confirming work readiness.
S696: Priority is highest for safety-critical parts and parts required to restore a turbine or electrical system to service.
S697: Parts supporting scheduled maintenance receive priority when their delivery date is necessary to protect an approved work window.
S698: Routine consumables are replenished according to agreed minimum and maximum stock levels.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
